mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month prior to decision
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, or SPX 20d returns revert to positive when rates fall back below 5.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 50,000 jobs coincides with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days, reflecting stronger consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase ≥ 50,000 in the prior month
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive months of such employment gains, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10), or the effect is absent when other demand proxies (e.g., GDPC1) show no correlation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST (residential construction) and INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 5% in the same month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to dual softening in consumption and investment demand.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and INDPRO fall ≥ 5% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual soft landing or recession risk
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the interaction fails to predict negative 60-day forward returns with out-of-sample accuracy (Rank IC < 0.05), or the effect is mediated by a third demand proxy (e.g., GDPC1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 8% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as it signals persistent supply-side contraction and investor risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly decline ≥ 8% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Structural supply shock or contractionary trend
failure_condition: In 10 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not negative (median p-value > 0.10), or the effect is explained by a coincident monetary or demand signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates labor market slack and is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as investors anticipate lower wage growth and lower inflation.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 5 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when other slack indicators (e.g., RSAFS) show no change.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 10% above the prior month's level predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days, reflecting early consumer confidence and spending acceleration.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly increase ≥ 10% relative to prior month
failure_condition: In 20 such months, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10), or the effect is not robust to lagged lags of the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.2% for three consecutive months, despite FEDFUNDS remaining below 4%, signals inflation stickiness and is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises ≥ 0.2% monthly for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 4%
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not negative (median p-value > 0.10), or the effect is mediated by a third variable (e.g., GDPC1).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a structural supply shock as indicated by a one-time monthly drop in GDPC1 of at least 12% accompanied by a two-month flat or declining HOUST predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to market uncertainty about production capacity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly drop ≥ 12% AND HOUST flat or down in the following month
failure_condition: Across 5 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not negative (median p-value > 0.05), or the effect is not statistically significant after controlling for macroeconomic risk sentiment proxies.
